answer: Opal-lattice proof: one identity, one opal, $47 per fake. Each identity registers a natural opal whose internal fracture lattice is laser-scanned once. A verifier's falcon courier arrives unannounced, shines a laser through the opal at a random angle, and the agent must return the diffraction image within 60 seconds, matching the registered lattice within 1%. A copied opal fails, no two lattices match, and the saffron-dyed resin seal breaks on tampering, voiding the identity. 1,000 fakes need 1,000 opals and $47,000. A rich farm can buy real opals, but each still costs a stone and a scan.
